page.title: Dashboard
page.purpose: Answer whether the runtime is doing its job, and route a reader to whatever went wrong. It leads with context avoided rather than inventory, because a count of sessions says nothing about whether the scenario is working.

priorities.statement: Context avoided leads. Inventory does not.
priorities.notes: '12 sessions active' is true and useless. Fetched versus materialized is the number that says whether the thesis holds, and it is also the PRD's acceptance signal — so the dashboard and the acceptance criteria agree by construction.

priorities.statement: Recent failures are one interaction from the failing line.
priorities.notes: The most common reason anyone opens this console is that a program failed. The dashboard's job is to shorten that path, not to summarize it.

priorities.statement: A human who has never seen this product can learn it here.
priorities.notes: The primary user is an agent, so a first-time reader has no mental model. The empty state is the teaching surface, not a placeholder.

priorities.statement: Binding coverage is visible without opening the registry.
priorities.notes: It is the ceiling on everything the runtime can do, and it moves as the fleet ships manifests.

priorities.statement: Nothing on the dashboard mounts the code editor.
priorities.notes: Snippets are static. The dashboard must stay fast enough to be the default route.

states.description: Thesis metric, recent failures, live sessions, and binding coverage are shown.
Nothing has run yet. The page explains what a program is, what a handle is, and why the runtime exists.
Some summaries resolved and others are unavailable; each states why.
Summaries are from a cached snapshot whose age is shown.
The summary could not be read and the reason is visible.

elements.name: Context avoided
elements.description: Fetched versus materialized across the corpus, with the window it covers.

elements.name: Recent failures
elements.description: Newest failing programs with their failure class, each linking to the failing line.

elements.name: Binding coverage
elements.description: Bound against total operation classes, with the manifest-coverage denominator.

elements.name: What Program Runtime is
elements.description: The teaching surface: a program replaces many tool calls, and a handle keeps results out of context.

claims.statement: The dashboard exposes a named region containing the thesis metric and recent failures.
Context avoided is the visually dominant element on the dashboard.
Context avoided is visible without scrolling at every declared viewport.
Each recent failure links directly to the program page positioned at its failing line, not to an unfiltered list.
claims.rationale: Triage is the spine journey. A link that lands on a list reintroduces the search this page exists to remove.

claims.statement: With nothing run yet, the dashboard explains what a program and a handle are rather than showing empty tiles.
claims.rationale: The product's user is an agent, so no human learns this by using it. If the empty state does not teach, nothing does.

claims.statement: A summary that could not be computed states why instead of rendering zero.
claims.rationale: Reporting an absence as zero misrepresents the runtime as idle rather than unmeasured.

claims.statement: Loading, empty, partial, stale, and error states each render dedicated content.
Recent failures, live sessions, and binding coverage are reachable by keyboard alone.
